pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships: Spencer Club Junior Lacross - Heathbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Partnerships: Spencer Club Junior Lacross
In the past few years, junior lacrosse has grown in southern England with the more established clubs adding junior programmes and working closely with local schools. The English Lacrosse Association has also encouraged local clubs by introducing local development officers to work in schools thus promoting lacrosse as a mixed gender PE activity.
Heathbrook has a long history of lacrosse being included in the curriculum and has particularly benefited from strong links with Spencer Lacrosse Club in Earlsfield. Heathbrook teams have regularly represented London and the South East in the National championships, winning the plate in 2010 and reaching the top 8 of UK schools in 2012. Our aim is to become National champions in the not too distant future!
Many pupils have benefitted from being able to add playing lacrosse at Regional and National level to their applications for secondary schools. Many have gone on to play at Junior/Senior level with Spencer Lacrosse Club, even joining tours of the UK and USA.
Have a look at the Spencer Lacrosse Club website. You can also find out about the English Lacrosse Association’s national pop lacrosse finals. In the meantime here’s a photo of our plate winning squad team 2014.

Partnerships
In order to provide the children with rich, varied and purposeful experiences, we have strong links with a number of partner organisations.
A New Direction
A New Direction works with teachers & schools to provide students with high-quality creative opportunities. A New Direction have delivered workshops at Heathbrook with supporting training for staff.
Clapham Pottery
Clapham Pottery is a busy self-funding and not-for-profit community pottery, offering pottery classes for all ages and abilities. Out children at Heathbrook are invited to take part in pottery sessions outside of school time.
Lambeth Music Service
Heathbrook are regular participants in the Lambeth Singing Festival. Our Rollingbrook school band also perform regularly on the Lambeth Music Stage at Lambeth Country Show.
Let’s Play
The Let’s Play program empowers teachers to embed creative learning across the whole curriculum. Let’s Play offers teachers and pupils the opportunity to see, make and learn through theatre. At Heathbrook the Year 6 children wrote playscripts to use in their performances.
London Philharmonic Orchestra
Heathbrook take part in the LPO BrightSparks concert, which offers inspiring live experiences for school audiences. Each year LPO perform for around 10,000 students with the chosen music and engaging presentation designed especially for school audiences. Concerts include a presenter breaking down the music in a fun and engaging way, and a big screen behind the Orchestra picks out key elements from the music or story
London Sinfonietta
Heathbrook have taken part in London Sinfonietta compostional challenge, as part of our Heathbrook Curriculum. Our fantastic work has been showcased in Royal Festival Hall and performed by London Sinfonietta.
London Youth Choir
London Youth Choir Experience works closely with school children, teachers, families and partner music hubs to establish and support singing in London’s local communities. Heathbrook participated in the London Youth Choir 10th anniversary performance, and some have the opportunity to join regional London Youth choirs.
National Trust
We are thrilled to be working collaboratively with the National Trust locally. 575 Wandsworth Road was the home of Khadambi Asalache for many years. Originally from Kenya, he was hugely talented particularly in the areas of writing, architecture and mathematics. Whilst he lived there, Khadambi transformed his house into a unique and stunning work of art mixing Islamic, English and African influences. When he died the National Trust decided to preserve 575 Wandsworth Road as he had left it.
Ominbus Theatre
Heathbrook children are regulars at Ominbus Theatre performances. We also have yearly invites to participate at the Clapham Lights event for the school choir and band.
PianoFunClub
PianoFunClub’s mission is to ensure that every child gets the chance to experience the magic of music lessons during school hours, at a price within the range of most families.
St. Paul’s Opera
St Paul’s deliver workshops at Heathbrook to introduce children to Opera. Heathbrook children are also invited to participate in performances.
Studio Voltaire
Heathbrook children attend workshops delivered by professionals at Studio Voltaire, as well as training for staff. Out Year 6 children are working on a year long project based around growth and transitions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships: Friends of Heathbrook Park - Heathbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Partnerships: Friends of Heathbrook Park
Heathbrook Park is the green space opposite Heathbrook School, which includes a playground and a large grass area surrounded by mature trees.
Over the past few years parents from the school have been using the park on an informal basis to mark the end of each term with a school picnic, sometimes involving art activities and games such as a tug of war. These have been very successful and happy events and every year the numbers of families attending them has grown.
Local parents have also instigated the planting of spring flower bulbs and the installing of picnic tables. It as become clear what an asset the park can be to the school, as a place to hold these regular events, as a sports day venue, as a safe and pleasant place for parents to play with their children after school.
Through these activities parents have formed strong links with the parks department of Wandsworth Council who manage the park, and this in turn has led to the forming of The Friends of Heathbrook Park, to include all those who use and enjoy the park: parents at Heathbrook School, dog-walkers and local residents.
The aim of The Friends of Heathbrook Park is to protect the natural beauty of the park and to initiate projects which will enhance the experience of all its users.
If you would like to join the Friends group, please contact Charlotte Hollinshead or Rebecca Hollweg via the school. We will be posting more information on this page soon.

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships: Heathbrook is an Associate School - Heathbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Partnerships: Heathbrook is an Associate School
Since September 2012 we have been an Associate School of the Southbank. Bea Colley who programmes many of their poetry performances and workshops is our key member of the Southbank team. This status allows us to take advantage of the amazing arts opportunities they can offer to associate schools. Children from Heathbrook took part in the first International Day of the Girl in November, sang in the Clore Ballroom for the Winter Festival and the Christmas markets and created ‘stained glass’ Christmas decorations that illuminated the Ballroom.
Another extraordinary privilege is having children participate in creating their own festival ‘Imagine’. A few children have been working with teams from other Associate schools to design exhibitions, activities and spaces for the Festival and create the ‘monsters’ that characterise the publicity materials. Heathbrook children will be performing at a range of events throughout the festival in the ‘Schools Take the Stage’, ‘Story Slam’, ‘Kids Takeover’, the ‘Imagine Festival Choir’ and the ‘Kids Debates’. Please check the Southbank website here for more details.
Later on in the year we will be taking part in Neighbourhood Festival and taking up a residency where some of lessons take place in spaces in the Southbank and we enjoy sessions in the poetry library and Voicelab.

pageCache.pageTitle: PTA Reading Volunteers - Heathbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
PTA Reading Volunteers
Our Vision and Values reflect our belief that the involvement of parents and carers in learning is key to the success of every child. We aim to achieve this by working in partnership with parents and carers. Parent and carer volunteers are an essential part of our community team at Heathbrook.
We have a thriving Reading Volunteers group consisting of parents, family and friends of Heathbrook, past and present. The Volunteers help Heathbrook children with their reading in many different ways; for example, they come in at different times of the day and support across the year groups from Reception up to Year 6. Some Volunteers work in the Library helping children choose books whilst others like to hear individual children reading.
The network of volunteers is very supportive and meets regularly, both formally and informally. If you are keen to find out more, please speak with Marion Guertin or come along to one of our gathering in the Library – look out for dates in our weekly newsletter.

On Wednesday 9th September, Stephanie White, our Senior Pastoral Lead, wrote to parents and carers of children starting Reception about Reception Before and After School Activities Autumn (first half) 2026.

Context and Rationale
Our Before and After School Activities are a key part of our commitment to providing exceptionally varied opportunities and stimulating children to Be the Best they can Be! They particularly focus on our four curriculum pillars of the Arts, Music, Outdoor Learning and Sport. We make full use of our extensive indoor and outdoor facilities, building on the strong relationships children have with adults. We do this by:
A waiting list system means that as many children as possible are able to access oversubscribed activities. Whilst we are aware that we cannot meet each child’s wishes every term, we aim to do so over time. Each half term we review the existing provision to look at ways we can make it even better next term. We actively seek and receive feedback from parents – please email activities@heathbrook.org if you have any comments or suggestions.

Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
The Breakfast Club is our own breakfast club and caters for all children from Nursery to Year 6. There is a range of gentle activities for them to enjoy as well as a selection of breakfast items. At the end of breakfast club, children go directly to their classes at 8.50am.
Breakfast Club is open from 7.30 to 8.50am. The daily cost is £4.50 per child.
Registration Process
We are extremely aware that our Breakfast Club and Heath Kidz After School Club are a vital provision for many of our parents. The pandemic has highlighted the importance of our flexible and needs-led process. We aim to do everything possible to meet the huge variety of situations that different families find themselves in.
Despite our best attempts to meet changing demand, a sudden unpredictable surge in bookings can be challenging for us to staff at short notice. On the odd occasion that you are unable to book a place, please contact a member of our office team. However there may be days when we cannot guarantee a place for every child.
Staff will continue to facilitate coffee mornings to gather parent views regularly about this provision and make further improvements. Previously parents have requested an advanced booking system and last moment places for sudden unexpected family situations.

Unfortunately, again due to staffing logistics, all booked places are non-returnable. For safeguarding reasons, places are non-transferable.
Note that a Terms and Conditions Form must be completed before any child can attend. When you have completed the form, please email admin@heathbrook.org in order to be invited to book via the Schoolgateway app.

pageCache.pageTitle: Holiday Heath Kidz - Heathbrook Primary School
pageCache.text:
Holiday Heath Kidz
Our aim is to provide an extended provision during holiday breaks that supports the community by providing affordable and safe childcare based on the school site and staffed by our experienced, friendly, Heathbrook staff. It is structured to keep children active, engaged and supported in a warm, inclusive environment.
It is an extension of the school’s Heath Kidz and Breakfast Club and is offered to Heathbrook pupils from Nursery to year 6.
This provision has been created in partnership with our parents and carers. Their considerable feedback and input has been invaluable.
Summer Holiday 2026
Here are the dates for the four weeks of our summer holiday programme:
Monday 20th – Friday 24th July Monday 27th – Friday 31st July Monday 3rd – Friday 7th August Monday 24th – Friday 28th August
Timings and cost
8am – 6pm: £45 daily rate 9am – 3pm: £37 daily rate
Sibling discount: £35 fee per child per day Full week discount: £10% off
Please note that no refunds can be issued for cancellations.
Pay via the Schoolgateway App. You can book from Monday 15th June. The closing date for bookings is Friday 10th July.
Daily timetable
8.00 – 9.00 Breakfast 10.00 Fruit snack 12.30 – 1.00 Packed lunch* 3.00 Part time close (£1 charge per minute for late collection) 4.30 Afternoon snack – sandwich/toast 6.00 Close (£1 charge per minute for late collection)
*Please provide your child with their own packed lunch – no nuts and please check for other allergens.
Daily Special Activity
(Taking place from 10am until 2pm)
Monday 20th July – Active Fun Tuesday 21st – Arty Day Wednesday 22nd – Crazy Crafting Thursday 23rd – Gymnastics and Games Friday 24th – Cooking
Monday 27th July – Park trip and parachute Tuesday 28th – Arty Day Wednesday 29th – Crazy Crafting Thursday 30th – Cooking Friday 31st – Active Fun
Monday 3rd August – Park trip and parachute Tuesday 4th – Arty Day Wednesday 5th – Gymnastics and Games Thursday 6th – Active Fun Friday 7th – Cooking
Monday 24th August – Active Fun Tuesday 25th – Arty Day Wednesday 26th – Crazy Crafting Thursday 27th – Active Fun Friday 28th – Cooking
Please make sure that your child dresses for the weather as there will be plenty of time for outdoor activities and play.
Frequently asked questions
How is this offer different to others operated by a franchise? Holiday Heath Kidz is run by Heathbrook staff for Heathbrook pupils only. This means that the pupils will know each other and the staff and will also benefit from being in a familiar environment.
Can I book my child in for the main activity only? Yes. The focus activity will run between 10am and 2pm, with a break for lunch. It is advised to book your child into the 9am to 3pm slot.
Can I book my child in for one day only? Yes. The offer is flexible.
My child has Free School Meals (FSM). Will a packed lunch be provided? No. All families eligible for FSM will receive funding for their child’s holiday lunches in advance through the voucher scheme.
What is for breakfast? A buffet including a choice of different cereals, toast, crumpets and pancakes.
What is for the afternoon snack? Healthy fruit options and/or a sandwich/toast.
Can my child eat snacks during the day? Fruit is provided mid-morning but children can bring their own fruit.
How are SEND pupils supported? In the same way that they are supported in Heath Kidz. Holiday Heath Kidz is not funded by the school budget or EHCP funding, which is strictly limited to school term time only. However, familiar pupils, staff and environment naturally reduces anticipatory anxiety. If you have a specific question about your child, please speak with Stephanie White, our Senior Pastoral Lead.
Will the age groups be mixed? The school uses the Hub, lower hall, middle hall, Art Room, playground and Wildlife Garden. Provision and supervision is adapted to the ages of the pupils.

Music
Music
Music at Heathbrook
At Heathbrook, music is a vital and valued part of our broad and balanced curriculum. Taught by our full time, specialist music teacher in our stunning, well equipped music room, our music education is designed to be inclusive, engaging, and inspiring for all pupils from Nursery to Year 6. We are committed to offering enriching experiences and ensuring equal access to music for all pupils.
We believe every child deserves a musical education, one that nurtures individual talent and develops musical aptitude. We place music at the heart of our bespoke community curriculum, recognising it as a powerful creative and social art form that should be enjoyed by all. Music not only brings joy, but also supports wider learning through skills such as listening, rhythm, coordination, cooperation, and confidence-building.
From Nursery upwards, children:
Above all, we aim to cultivate a lifelong love of music, where every child can succeed, express themselves, and find joy through their musical journey.
To find out more, read our Intent, Implementation and Impact statement.
Lead School Status – we have recently obtained Lead School Status by Lambeth Music Services, which recognises the importance that Heathbrook places on creative education, especially music.
listen to and appreciate various genres
learn about the history of music
Instrumental Lessons
All children have access to playing a musical instrument through their whole class ensemble teaching from year 2 onwards. In addition, we offer a range of instrumental lessons, which are very popular and take place during the school day. These are taught by peripatetic teachers from within and outside of school and includes; violin, guitar, flute, clarinet, trumpet and keyboard.
Singing
Singing is an important part of our school lives. Children take part in weekly singing assemblies, sing as part of class routines, take part in infant and junior choir and have the opportunity to sing out of school in prestigious venues such as the Royal Festival Hall and Royal Albert Hall.
CHOIR (yrs 5/6) – Please click on link for Lambeth singing concert material – youtube sing-a-long videos
Performances
At Heathbrook, we offer a rich variety of performance opportunities throughout the year, allowing children to share and celebrate their talents. Highlights include:
Rolling Brook, our school band, made up of children from Year5&6 and have regular gigs at the Clapham Lights event and the Lambeth Country Show, with Lambeth Sounds (Lambeth Music Services).
Enrichment
We endeavour to give the children as many opportunities to see and take part in musical events as possible. We take part in the Lambeth Music Festival, Lambeth Country Show, BrightSparks concerts, Primary Proms and as an associate school, we take part in events at the Southbank Centre. We nurture partnerships with our local arts organisations, such as, Lambeth Music Services, St Paul’s opera and the Omnibus theatre.
There are a variety of extra curricular musical activities carried out by our music specialist including; percussion club, choirs for infants and juniors, songwriting club, orchestra and our school band, Rolling Brook.
Music Technology
We inspire creativity through digital tools like Soundtrap and Chrome Music Lab and promote collaborative composition in group settings.

Headteacher’s Welcome
As Headteacher, I welcome you to our primary school in Lambeth. We take pride in creating an environment where every opportunity is offered to inspire children to learn.
Our school vision is very clear:
We believe in energising children to become lifelong learners as partners in a thriving learning community where each child aspires to achieve their dreams.
We are dedicated to providing an emotionally enabling and creative environment. This is underpinned by strong trusting relationships between staff, pupils, parents, carers, governors and local partners. We honour the uniqueness of every child.
We believe in stimulating children to be the best they can be and develop a love of learning in its widest sense. To achieve this we provide exceptionally varied opportunities including an amazing outdoor environment and our extremely creative Community Curriculum.
In addition to our high expectations for English and maths, children enjoy playing in our orchestra, inventing in our art studio and participating in a wide range of sports locally. Strong relationships with our families lie at the heart of everything we do and we have a thriving Parent Teacher Association (Friends of Heathbrook Primary) that supports our vision and values.
Ours is a caring school where the children are warmly received and encouraged throughout their time with us to ‘aim high’, fulfil their potential and engage with all the opportunities the school has to offer. We firmly believe that for this to be best achieved we must establish a genuine partnership between home and school. We pride ourselves on open communication, so if you have any questions or comments regarding the website or any other matter, please do not hesitate to contact the office, your child’s classteacher or me.
We work closely with parents and carers, partners and the wider community to ensure the success of our children. We believe that your children deserve the best possible chances in life and that they learn best when there are strong links between home and school.
We are proud of our school and the achievements of our students. I hope this website gives you a sense of that with useful information that you may need as a parent every day.
Mr Ben Roberts Headteacher

Our Governors
“The headteacher, senior leaders, governing body and staff have a shared vision for the type of education they want to provide.” (Ofsted June 2016)
Along with all schools, we have a Governing Body. Our Governing Body comprises of parents, members of the local community and staff.
The Governing Body has a key role to play in making improvements to our school and raising standards. Working within a complex legislative framework, governing bodies are required to promote high standards of educational achievement. They meet this requirement through strategic planning, target setting, monitoring, evaluation, policy development, review and performance management.
Working in partnership with the Headteacher and other staff, the Governing Body’s responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Our Main Committee delegates many of its responsibilities to its Achievement, Resources, Wellbeing and Pay Sub-Committees, whilst a Steering Group also meets regularly. The meeting attendance records demonstrate our governors’ commitment to the school.

Parent Forums
The aims of our Parent Forums are to:
• enable parents and carers to meet, share ideas and feed back to the school • give parents and carers a voice and enable them to contribute to school decision-making • help develop the partnership between parents and carers and the school • consult parents and carers and advise the governing body of parents and carers’ views.
